subject.title: [Feature] Pre-response enforcement hooks (hard gates) for mandatory tool-call / policy rules

question: Should OpenClaw add a fail-closed response-gate API, and what validator trust, retry/fallback, audit, plugin permission, and config semantics should define that security boundary?
rationale: Source inspection proves the missing seam, but the permanent behavior changes security and product semantics across final output delivery, plugin APIs, and high-stakes operator workflows.

options.title: Design a versioned response-gate API
options.body: Approve a maintainer-led core/plugin design for mandatory tool ledgers, typed validators, fail-closed finalization, bounded retries, deterministic fallbacks, and audit records while keeping domain policy packs plugin-owned.

options.title: Keep current hooks advisory
options.body: Document that OpenClaw supports pre-tool blocking and outbound cancellation but does not guarantee mandatory pre-response validation in core.

options.title: Split narrower enforcement tracks
options.body: Keep this issue as the umbrella but land only separately reviewed pieces such as tool confirmation, fake-tool enforcement, or outbound send policy when their contracts are ready.

recommendation.title: Design a versioned response-gate API
recommendation.body: Approve a maintainer-led core/plugin design for mandatory tool ledgers, typed validators, fail-closed finalization, bounded retries, deterministic fallbacks, and audit records while keeping domain policy packs plugin-owned.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans security defaults, product scope, and final-response/plugin API boundaries, and steipete has prior review context plus adjacent reply-dispatch history.
